smt-2012-advanced-tiebreaker-01.prompt: Let $p(n)$ be the smallest digit that is part of the decimal writing of a natural number $n$. Compute $p(100)+p(101)+p(102)+\dots+p(998)+p(999)$.

smt-2012-advanced-tiebreaker-02.prompt: We define $n$ to be a *squarefree* integer if, for every prime $p$, $p^2$ does not divide $n$. Let $f(n)$ be the sum of the reciprocals of all the divisors of $n$. We define $n$ to be an *amazing* integer if $f(n)=2$. How many squarefree amazing integers are there?

smt-2012-advanced-tiebreaker-03.prompt: There are $7$ cages in a row in an animal shelter and an ample supply of three different kinds of animals: dogs, cats, and golden bears. Since golden bears do not like each other, they cannot be placed in adjacent cages. Cats also do not like each other (but not as much so as golden bears), so there cannot be more than two cats in a row. How many ways are there to fill the cages with animals?
